text: “hare kṛṣṇa hare kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa hare hare
hare rāma hare rāma rāma rāma hare hare”
translation: Lord Gaurasundar sings in a very sweet voice, “Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare, Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare.”

text: gṛhe thāka, vane thāka, sadā ‘hari’ bale’ ḍāka
sukhe duḥkhe bhulo nāka, vadane hari-nām kara re
translation: Whether you live at home or in the forest, always chant the Lord’s Holy Name; in happiness or sadness, don’t forget – chant the Holy Name and fill your lips with Harināma.

text: māyā-jāle baddha haye, āchha michhe kāja laye
ekhan-o chetana peye, rādhā-mādhav-nām bala re
translation: Bound in māyā’s net, you’ve slaved and toiled in vain. But now that you have a human life and consciousness, chant the Lord’s Name, “Rādhā-Mādhava.”

text: jīvana ha-ila śeṣa, nā bhajile hṛṣīkeśa
translation: This life must surely end soon, and you have not worshipped Hṛṣīkeśa, the master of the senses. Bhakti Vinod advises: at least once, taste the Nāma-rasa, the nectar of the Holy Name.
